chunks.agentNotes: This chunk was mostly a broad reference page on fel magic rather than a narrative page. Reused existing entities for Kael'thas, Rommath, Liadrin, Lor'themar, blood elves, Dalaran, and Kirin Tor; created only the broad Lore entity 'fel' after variant searches showed no existing general match. Avoided creating many incidental entities from gallery/reference lists and navboxes.
chunks.summary: Extracted the fel article's main conceptual entity as Lore 'fel' and updated existing blood elf-related entities with source-scoped observations about ambient demonic reconstruction, green eyes, Kael'thas's personal fel turn, and Dalaran/Kirin Tor opposition to fel study.
chunks.title: 8 References + 34 sections

chunks.agentNotes: No new entities or links recorded in this chunk because the visible material largely reiterates already-ingested people, groups, places, and concepts from prior blood elf/high elf chunks. Potentially new mentions such as Ban'dinoriel, Convocation of Silvermoon, Talanas Windrunner, Thoradin, Arathor/Strom, Zanza, Amani/Zul'Aman, Council of Tirisfal, Archmage Maenius, Zin-Malor, Mehlar Dawnblade, Vandellor, Belo'vir, Astalor Bloodsworn, Anveena Teague, A'dal, Sha'tar, Magus Rimtori, Hawkhelm, and Hex Lord Malacrass were not extracted here to avoid over-creating from a reference-heavy overview chunk without follow-up coverage.
chunks.summary: This chunk spans major high elf and blood elf history from the founding of Quel'Thalas through the Sunwell's rebirth, but most entities and themes were already covered earlier in the ingest. It reinforces Dath'Remar's founding of the Sunwell and Quel'Thalas, the anti-detection runestone barrier Ban'dinoriel, the Convocation of Silvermoon, early ranger origins under Talanas Windrunner, the Troll Wars alliance with Arathor, Dalaran and Kirin Tor ties, the Second and Third War devastation, the rise of the sin'dorei, Kael'thas's fel corruption, M'uru and the Blood Knights, Horde admission, and Sunwell restoration.
chunks.title: 10 References

chunks.agentNotes: Searched before creating. Reused same-job entities for major recurring blood elf leaders. Found existing project entities for Sunreavers and Quel'Danas and recorded source-scoped observations instead of duplicating. Skipped many one-off minor names, territories, and factions in this dense chunk to prefer fewer stronger entities.
chunks.summary: Expanded the blood elf page with major source-scoped updates on Lor'themar's long regency, Halduron's Sunwell gatekeeping and military role, Aethas's Dalaran diplomacy and purge fallout, Rommath's anti-Void stance and crisis leadership, Liadrin's public anti-addiction rhetoric and later campaigns, and the Sunreavers' arc from Kirin Tor admission to purge, Onslaught, and War Within defense. Also recorded Quel'Danas as a fortified and repeatedly besieged Sunwell island, and created new entities for Eressea Dawnsinger, Malithas Brightblade, Thalorien Dawnseeker, Blood-Queen Lana'thel, Magister Umbric, Spellbreaker Maella, Silvermoon Court, and Convocation of Silvermoon.
chunks.title: Part 182

chunks.agentNotes: No new entities were created. Avoided creating Suramar/Thalyssra because they were not yet necessary for a strong source-scoped capture in this chunk and would have required project search before creation. The chunk transitions into the separate Timeline page afterward, but this excerpt is only the preface/table of contents and did not yet warrant extraction.
chunks.summary: This chunk closes the Quel'Thalas kingdom page with external politics, notes/trivia, and a speculation section. Recorded source-scoped updates that Quel'Thalas remained aligned with the Horde through the rebellions against two corrupt Warchiefs and is represented on the Horde Council by its regent lord; that post-Nightfallen relations with Suramar are framed as a mutual Highborne-kingdom alliance culminating in the marriage of the two realms' leaders; and that the page presents unresolved succession after the Sunstrider dynasty as speculation, naming Lor'themar's refusal to found a new dynasty, Rommath and Halduron as possible successors, and a wording discrepancy around Anasterian as the 'last king.' Also captured the page's trivia-style note that Quel'Thalas is one of the only Horde-aligned states explicitly called a kingdom here, plus non-narrative notes on inconsistent pre-Third War color depictions.
chunks.title: Part 183 + 93 sections

chunks.agentNotes: No new entities created. Given the chunk's encyclopedic breadth and heavy overlap with already touched entities, I avoided low-value duplicate updates and focused on chunk summary only.
chunks.summary: This chunk is a broad Warcraft timeline page spanning cosmology through early World of Warcraft. Most entities and events already exist or were covered earlier in the ingest. It reinforces previously recorded source-scoped observations for entities such as the Sunwell, Kel'Thuzad, Arthas, Kael'thas, Lor'themar, Vereesa, Korialstrasz, Wildhammer, Horde, Silver Hand, and Quel'Thalas, but does not add many chunk-specific details that warrant new entities or job updates beyond already captured history.
chunks.title: 20 References + 11 sections

chunks.agentNotes: Skipped creating a large number of one-off timeline entities from unrelated factions, dungeons, and raids because they would add low-value noise relative to this ingest's established blood elf/high elf focus. Reused existing project entities where clear search hits existed; no new entities were necessary for the chunk's strongest relevant material.
chunks.summary: This chunk is a broad Warcraft timeline spanning early WoW through the end of The Burning Crusade and into Wrath of the Lich King. Most timeline beats are too diffuse for efficient extraction, so I focused on the strong blood elf-relevant material: Kael'thas's Outland/Tempest Keep/Sunwell arc, M'uru's capture and sacrificial restoration role, the founding and later moral shift of the Blood Knights under Liadrin and Rommath, Lor'themar's blocked warning about Anveena, Voren'thal's defection to form the Scryers, the blood elves joining the Horde, and the Shattered Sun Offensive campaign on Quel'Danas.
chunks.title: 25 [ 246 ] + 2 sections

chunks.agentNotes: No new entities created. The chunk contains many major timeline events and figures, but most were outside this ingest's current focus or too broad to justify duplicative low-value entity creation from a single timeline summary.
chunks.summary: This chunk is a broad Cataclysm through Warlords of Draenor timeline. Most events are too diffuse for efficient extraction, so I focused on blood-elf-adjacent and already-tracked entities: Jaina, Aethas, Dalaran, and the Kirin Tor during Theramore, the Divine Bell affair, and the Purge of Dalaran, plus a high-level Horde political update through Garrosh's fall and Vol'jin's succession.
chunks.title: 28 [ 368 ] [ Notes 4 ] + 3 sections

chunks.agentNotes: Most remaining timeline mentions were too diffuse for efficient entity creation in this chunk. Search results for Magni Bronzebeard, Anduin Wrynn, Xal'atath, Dark Heart, and Thalyssra did not yield clean, confident matches worth creating or linking within this pass given chunk density and the instruction to prefer fewer, stronger entities.
chunks.summary: This timeline chunk spans Legion through The War Within. I focused on updating already-touched or clearly matched entities rather than creating many broad timeline nodes: Khadgar, the Council of Six, Dalaran, the Kirin Tor, Turalyon, Alleria, Arator, Umbric, and Khaz Algar-area locations including Azj-Kahet, Dornogal, Isle of Dorn, and Khaz Algar. Key source-scoped additions include Dalaran's Legion-era relocations and final destruction by Xal'atath using the Dark Heart, the Council of Six's decision to teleport Dalaran to the Isle of Dorn, Alleria's Sunwell incident and role in void elf origins, Umbric's transformation context, and Khaz Algar as the central War Within campaign theater.
chunks.title: 32 [ 550 ] [ 551 ] [ 552 ] + 4 sections

chunks.agentNotes: Focused extraction on strong recurring or blood-elf-relevant entities rather than every patch/delve/dungeon title. Reused same-job entities for Arator, Alleria, Umbric, Turalyon, Lor'themar, Liadrin, Halduron, Quel'Danas, Zul'Aman, Light's Hope Chapel, and the Light; created new entities for Xal'atath, Locus-Walker, Ve'nari, Danath Trollbane, Faerin Lothar, Azir, Nexus-King Salhadaar, Marran Trollbane, Zul'jarra, Lothraxion, Decimus, Devouring Host, K'aresh Trust, Red Dawn, Sureki, Vanguard of the Light, Twilight's Blade, K'aresh, Hallowfall, Arathi Highlands, Harandar, Voidstorm, Dark Heart, Dimensius, L'ura, Darkwell, and Dawnwell. Avoided creating many secondary figures and generic patch labels.
chunks.summary: This future-timeline chunk centers on Xal'atath's cross-patch arc from Undermine through K'aresh into Midnight, plus the Red Dawn/Stromgarde conflict and major Quel'Thalas-facing Midnight developments around the Sunwell, Arator, Liadrin, Umbric, Halduron, the Voidstorm, Darkwell, and Dawnwell.

chunks.agentNotes: The timeline portion is reference-heavy and too diffuse for efficient extraction. The actionable material begins at the Kael'thas page, which primarily reinforces and expands an already-touched same-job entity rather than introducing new distinct entities in this chunk.
chunks.summary: This chunk is mostly a timeline references section plus the start of the Kael'thas Sunstrider page. I updated Kael'thas with a consolidated source-scoped character-page summary covering his succession after Anasterian, renaming of the sin'dorei, fall to Kil'jaeden and the Legion, defeat at Quel'Danas and Magisters' Terrace, and later Revendreth/Venthyr repentance arc.
chunks.title: Part 302 + 45 sections

chunks.agentNotes: Most additional named mentions here are diffuse biographical cameos within Kael'thas's long page. To avoid low-value sprawl, I did not create many one-off nodes for figures such as Lirath Windrunner, Lord Saltheril, Sathera, Othmar Garithos, Jailor Kassan, Magroth the Defender, Priestess Delrissa, Anveena Teague, the Accuser, or various Shadowlands/nathrezim names. Many core entities already existed in the same-job roster, so I favored updating those rather than creating new entities or links.
chunks.summary: This chunk is the main body of the Kael'thas biography page. I used it primarily to substantially expand Kael'thas's source-scoped character arc from prince and Council of Six mage through the fall of Quel'Thalas, destruction of the corrupted Sunwell, regency arrangements, Outland campaigns, fel corruption, M'uru capture, Sunwell return attempt, death, and Revendreth redemption. I also recorded focused same-job updates for Lor'themar, Rommath, M'uru, the Sunwell, and the blood elves where the page gave strong role/history reinforcement.
chunks.title: 15 External links + 1 sections

chunks.agentNotes: Most additional names in this chunk were either already touched in this job or appeared in non-canon/trivia/reference/gallery/navbox material, so I avoided creating low-value duplicates. I treated RPG/Hearthstone/April Fools/development/trivia material as supporting context only and kept core updates centered on the main lore presentations.
chunks.summary: This chunk finishes the Kael'thas page and starts the Sunwell page. I updated Kael'thas with a source-scoped synthesis of his personality, motives, fall into fel corruption, and Shadowlands-era remorse/redemption arc, plus his tensions with Anasterian and self-justifying devotion to Silvermoon. I also updated the Sunwell with a consolidated dedicated-page arc: Dath'Remar's creation of it, Arthas/Kel'Thuzad's corruption of it, Kael'thas's destruction of it, Velen's restoration of it, and its later Darkwell/Dawnwell transformations in Midnight material.
chunks.title: 5 126,466 + 20 sections

chunks.agentNotes: Most named entities in this chunk were already touched earlier in the ingest, so I avoided redundant updates and did not extract from speculation, gallery, patch metadata, or external-link/reference material except where the main prose clearly added useful Sunwell-wide synthesis.
chunks.summary: This final chunk is mostly the Sunwell page’s later sections plus references/external links. I used it to substantially consolidate the Sunwell’s source-scoped page summary: its creation by Dath'Remar from Well of Eternity water, its role as the magical and cultural heart of Thalassian society, its corruption and destruction in the Third War, restoration and Light infusion via Velen and M'uru, and its later Darkwell/Dawnwell transformations in Midnight.

Burning Crystal

From Warcraft Wiki

Jump to navigation
Jump to search
Not to be confused with Fel crystal  or Mana crystal .

A large Burning Crystal.

The Burning Crystals are crystals found on Sunstrider Isle , to the west of the Sunspire in Eversong Woods . They have long been used to power the isle's experimentations. The mana wyrms were their guardians, until the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas drove them errant from the blood elves' lack of magical control over them. [ 1 ]

The unchecked power of the Burning Crystals negatively influenced the isle's wildlife population and natural balance. For example, the nearby lynxes succumbed to the influence of the crystals, prompting the blood elves to put them down. [ 2 ] The blood elves at the Sunspire will continue trying to rein in the Burning Crystals. [ 3 ]

Speculation

This article or section includes speculation, observations or opinions possibly supported by lore or by Blizzard officials. It should not be taken as representing official lore.

Although not called that, based on their appearance, they may be fel crystals . As these crystals have been present since before the Scourge sacking as noted above and would therefore not be powered by demonic energies, as the blood elves did not turn to using demonic energy until long after Arthas' attack. It is possible that Magistrix Erona may be lying about their nature. Another possibility is that this corruption could be attributed to the blood elves substituting the powering of these crystals with demonic fel energy, which may or may not be a secret kept from civilians, while the crystals themselves were there long before.

From Warcraft Wiki

This article is about the blood elves' lore. For the playable race, see Blood elf (playable) . For elves in general, see Elf .
Blood elves

Artwork of a pair of blood elves by Forrest Imel .

“We must put this misery behind us. We must enter a new chapter! And so I say to you that, as of this day, we are no longer high elves ! In honor of the blood that was shed throughout this kingdom, in honor of the sacrifices of our brothers and sisters, our parents, and our children, in honor of Anasterian ... as of this day we will take the name of our royal lineage! As of this day, we are sin'dorei! For Quel'Thalas !”

— Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider proclaims the rise of the blood elves [ 4 ]
The blood elves (or sin'dorei , "children of the blood" in Thalassian — pronounced [ˈsiːndɔraɪ] , [siːnˈdɔraɪ] or [siːndɔreɪ] ) are high elves who changed their name after the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas . [ 5 ] Their new name is a dirge, referencing both the blood of their many brethren who fell during the Third War , and their royal lineage . [ 4 ] [ 6 ]

For nearly 7,000 years, high elven society centered on the sacred Sunwell , a magical fount that was created using a vial of pure arcane energy from the first Well of Eternity . Nourished and strengthened by its potent energies, the enchanted kingdom of Quel'Thalas prospered within the verdant forests north of Lordaeron . During the Third War, however, Arthas Menethil and the Scourge slaughtered almost ninety percent of the population, then used the Sunwell to resurrect Archlich Kel'Thuzad , irrevocably tainting the fount in the process. When Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider rushed to his homeland's aid, he renamed the survivors into the "blood elves" in honor of their fallen people, [ 7 ] then destroyed the corrupted Sunwell. The sin'dorei, however, had grown addicted to its energies and were left weakened and despondent without them. Before his departure, the Sun King left Quel'Thalas in the hands of his regent, Lor'themar Theron , while he traveled to avenge his people and find a cure to sate their hunger for magic.

The blood elves strove to rebuild Quel'Thalas and reclaimed much of their land from the Scourge. Although Kael'thas had assured his people that one day he would return to Quel'Thalas and lead them to paradise, yet time revealed that his promises were nothing more than lies. On the broken world of Outland , the lord of the blood elves was twisted due to his reliance on fel energy, and eventually came under the sway of the Burning Legion 's supreme commander, Kil'jaeden . During the battle for Quel'Danas , the mad prince sought to usher his new master into Azeroth through a Sunwell restored but defiled, and was ultimately killed by the Shattered Sun Offensive . Prophet Velen of the draenei later used the essence of the naaru M'uru to purify the Sunwell as a fount of both arcane and holy energy. [ 8 ]

Inspired by the Sunwell's rebirth, the blood elves have since entered into a shining new era in their ancient race's history. Although some remain hesitant to abandon their dependence on arcane magic, others have embraced change for the betterment of Quel'Thalas with the encouragement of Regent Lord Lor'themar. [ 5 ] Despite the numerous tragedies of their past, the blood elves continue to stand strong and endure, tenaciously striving to restore their beloved nation's past glory. [ 9 ] Reinvigorated, they fight to protect Quel'Thalas, conquer their magic addiction, and help redeem the soul of their ancient people. [ 10 ]

History
Main article: High elf

Icon of Blood

In the centuries following the War of the Ancients , the night elves adopted druidism and outlawed the practice of arcane magic, which became punishable by death. However, many Highborne who survived the Great Sundering grew restless, since they viewed magic as their birthright and suffered from magical withdrawal . At their head, Dath'Remar Sunstrider chafed at the restrictions that weighed on his kind, and they eventually began to practice the arcane arts without fear or restraint. Around 7,300 BDP , the kaldorei could not bring themselves to put so many of their kin to death, and instead exiled the reckless Highborne from their lands, cutting them off from the Well of Eternity 's energies on Mount Hyjal . Glad to be rid of their conservative cousins and free to practice the arcane with impunity, [ 11 ] Dath'Remar and the Highborne built a fleet of mighty ships and set sail upon the seas until they made landfall on a new continent some years later, which would one day become known as the Eastern Kingdoms . [ 12 ]

In 6,800 BDP, when they reached the nexus of ley lines they had been seeking since their arrival, Dath'Remar poured a vial of water from the Well of Eternity into a small lake at the center of the nexus. A brilliant fount of energy tore through the skies of Azeroth , which the Highborne dubbed this glorious cradle of power the Sunwell ; a name chosen in honor of Dath'Remar and his bold quest to reignite their culture. They called their new land Quel'Thalas or "High Home" in Thalassian , and declared that it would dwarf the late Kaldorei Empire and stand as a monument for the ages. [ 13 ] In time, they would even be known by a new name: high elves , and from that point on, all had access to the Sunwell's powers from anywhere on Azeroth. Over time, the Sunwell's unique energies became part of them acutely, and they came to regard its waters as holy. [ 14 ] The elves then prospered for thousands of years in their enchanted kingdom, under the rule of the Sunstrider dynasty and the Convocation of Silvermoon . Although they were constantly at war with a grudging foe, the Amani trolls of Zul'Aman , to whom they had colonized their lands [ 15 ] - the mighty kingdom of Quel'Thalas stood strong for 7,000 years to come.

Fall of Quel'Thalas
Main article: Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas
During the Third War in 20 ADP, Arthas Menethil and the Scourge invaded Quel'Thalas , corrupting the Sunwell after the ressurection of Kel'Thuzad . Despite their best efforts, most of the queldorei population was eradicated during the conflict, leaving only about ten percent after the genocide. When Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider returned from Dalaran , he rallied the survivors and attended his father's funeral, succeeding him as leader of a kingdom on the brink of extinction. The survivors greeted their prince with thinly veiled resentment, and Kael'thas made no excuses for being absent in Quel'Thalas's hour of need. [ 16 ] In remembrance of their fallen brethren, the survivors renamed themselves as the "sin'dorei" ("children of the blood" in Thalassian ), and swore to avenge their fallen race. Upon discovering that the Sunwell had been tainted by necromantic energies , Prince Kael'thas concluded that the fount had to be destroyed before it could kill them all. With the aid of the most powerful remaining Magisters , who had come to the same conclusion, Kael'thas destroyed the Sunwell through a great ritual, [ 4 ] however, it also resulted in a withdrawal-based lethargy for the elven race. [ 5 ]

A blood mage fighting the undead forces of the Scourge .

Prior to his departure, Kael'thas commanded his regent, Lor'themar Theron , to safeguard the elven homeland, while Halduron Brightwing was named the new Ranger-general of Silvermoon . The elven prince then took fifteen percent of their remaining forces, including some of his most powerful and gifted magisters, to fight alongside the Alliance resistance across the ruins of Lordaeron . [ 17 ] This tenuous alliance, however, would not last under the bigoted scrutiny of Othmar Garithos , a human who had felt wronged by the high elves' conduct in the past. The grand marshal consistently gave the blood elves either meager tasks beneath their capabilities, or worse, suicidal missions devoid of reinforcements in order to rid himself of the sin'dorei. [ 18 ] Kael'thas and his forces were eventually offered aid from an unlikely source: the naga under Lady Vashj , who shared a common ancestry with the elves and a common enemy in the Scourge. When Garithos discovered this alliance, the blood elves were imprisoned in the Dungeons of Dalaran and sentenced to death for "conspiring with the enemy", until they escaped with the aid of the naga. [ 19 ]

In the extra-dimensional wastes of Outland , the remnants of Draenor , Kael'thas beseeched Illidan Stormrage for a cure to the blood elves' addiction to magic. The Betrayer had a different proposal in mind, though: in return for the blood elves' loyalty, he would teach them to drain magic from powerful alternative sources, including demons. [ 20 ] It was an offer Kael'thas felt he had to accept; he was certain his people would die without either a cure or a new source of magic. [ 21 ] After they conquered the broken world, the Sunfury blood elves followed Illidan to the Icecrown Glacier in an attempt to destroy the Lich King ; however, they were defeated by Arthas who wounded Illidan with Frostmourne , forcing the blood elves and naga to retreat. [ 22 ] [ 23 ] During the battles in Northrend , several of the deceased blood elves, including the powerful bearer of Quel'Delar , Lana'thel , were raised into undeath by Arthas, to serve him as his " San'layn ". [ 24 ]

In Quel'Thalas, the blood elves were undergoing their own tribulations. Retaking their homeland seemed a daunting task, as the Scourge was still occupying it in large numbers, and the kingdom was still a wasteland. Weakened by their addiction to magic, the general blood elf populace relied heavily on the Farstriders for protection, who were relatively unaffected by the withdrawal. [ 4 ]

Rise of the sin'dorei
Main article: Quel'Thalas (kingdom)

The towering spires and lush forests of Quel'Thalas , the elven homeland rebuilt after the Third War .

In time, Prince Kael'thas sent back Grand Magister Rommath and a group of magisters to Quel'Thalas, to spread Illidan's teachings (smoothly attributed to Kael) and to reclaim Quel'Thalas with their powerful magic. They also passed a message of hope for the survivors, that one day Kael'thas would return to lead his people to paradise. Invigorated by the formidable new techniques at their disposal, such as forcibly taking the magic and power of arcane-bearing creatures, the blood elves were able to retake much of Eversong Woods and even restore much of Silvermoon City . Unlike their brethren on Outland, the blood elves of Azeroth employed this technique only on mana crystals and small mana-bearing vermin. [ 25 ] Others were not content with this and traveled south to the Ghostlands in order to drive the undead from Quel'Thalas. The blood elves were encouraged to deal with their magical addiction sensibly and with good judgment, to walk the line between deficiency and overindulgence . [ 4 ] The remaining Scourge eventually proved little match for the Magisters, who then rebuilt the city "almost overnight." Emboldened by the notion of the prince's promised return to lead his people to power and glory, the blood elves began to focus on regaining all of their homeland and their strength to this end. [ 7 ]

Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider , lord of the blood elves.

Meanwhile, the blood elves in Outland under Prince Kael'thas dispersed—most, such as the powerful Sunfury forces, remained with the prince and took over the mana-rich area of the Netherstorm . Others, such as the Eclipsion , traveled to serve Illidan Stormrage 's ambitions in Shadowmoon Valley . Several were trained as demon hunters under the Betrayer himself. They were sons, daughters, mothers, and fathers. Some were trained in the arts of war, others were simple artisans, but one thing they had in common was the hatred that burned in their souls. They had all lost someone to the Legion, and they were all consumed by a need for vengeance. Each were forced to eat the flesh of a demon and bind their spirit with the creature. The elves transformed, sprouting horns and wings much like Illidan's, and from that point on, each demon hunter would fight an inner struggle against the monster that lurked in their soul. The success rate of this training was mixed: some were driven to insanity, while others fully succeeded in their training and became elite members of Illidan's retinue. [ 26 ]

When Illidan decided to strike against Shattrath City , believing the naaru 's holdings could threaten his own sovereignty over Outland , [ 27 ] he left the matter to Prince Kael'thas and his blood elves. Under the leadership of Voren'thal the Seer , an elder magister and advisor to the prince, a Sunfury contingent moved towards Shattrath City. En route to the battle, Voren'thal was struck by a vision that forever changed him: his homeland of Quel'Thalas , restored to its golden glory by the grace of a radiant light; and his people, at last freed from the shackles of addiction and despair, their torments eased by the naaru from whence flowed this Holy Light . The magister shared this vision with his followers, who began to consider that their race's salvation lay not with their increasingly volatile prince or the capricious Betrayer, but with the very naaru they'd been commanded to slay. As the regiment of blood elves approached Shattrath, the unexpected happened - the blood elves put down their weapons before the Aldor defenders. During an audience with the naaru A'dal , Voren'thal pledged himself and his followers to the cause of the Sha'tar . Their defection was the largest loss ever incurred by Kael'thas' forces, as many of the strongest and brightest scholars and magisters had been swayed by Voren'thal's influence. They became known as the Scryers . [ 28 ]

Publicly, Kael'thas condemned the act as treason and an attack on his sovereignty as prince. Privately, he saw Voren'thal's defection as evidence of his own failure. This incident widened the rift between the prince and the Lord of Outland, who paid little attention to Voren'thal's army. Under the influence of Kil'jaeden , Kael'thas lost all faith in his former master and looked to the demon lord as a new benefactor. The prince knew that he should not trust the Burning Legion , especially after what it had done to his kingdom, but he could not resist the temptation of fel magic. In return, Kil'jaeden granted the prince what he sought most: more knowledge about using fel magic, but also promised him salvation for his people and ultimate power. [ 29 ] In secret, Kael'thas began harvesting the great power coursing through the Netherstorm, and his judgment—and actions—became increasingly callous, notably when he ordered the slaughter of the people of Kirin'Var Village . [ 30 ]

Despite his allegiance to Kil'jaeden, Kael'thas still cared for his people and decided that the naaru M'uru he captured at Tempest Keep power could sate the elves' cravings for magic. However, his people had mixed feelings and were troubled by the idea of leeching energy from a being of the Holy Light. Others experimented on it for months until they learned how to force out its holy energies to wield the Light themselves. In addition to their traditional Magisters and Farstriders, the blood elves expanded their power base with the Blood Knights , a group of paladins under the lead of Lady Liadrin . [ 4 ] [ 31 ]

Having rebuilt much of their kingdom, the blood elves looked to finding new allies. They had once been part of the Alliance of Lordaeron, but the Alliance no longer cared to defend Quel'Thalas. [ 7 ] The blood elves were offered aid from an unexpected source: the free-willed Forsaken undead. The blood elves were initially wary of their intentions, fearing a trick; but the elves eventually acquiesced, as no one else was willing to fight for Quel'Thalas at all. [ 7 ] [ 32 ] Their aid included reinforcements, a number of outposts in and around the reclaimed blood elf territories, and a teleportation device between the Undercity and Silvermoon. The Banshee Queen Sylvanas Windrunner herself later claimed to have retained a great love for her homeland and its people. [ 33 ]

World of Warcraft

This section concerns content related to the original World of Warcraft .

A few years after the Third War , some blood elves continued to leave Quel'Thalas and travel across Azeroth , such as Ferelyn Bloodscorn who joined the Argent Dawn to fight against the Scourge . [ 34 ] An expedition led by Magus Rimtori notably traveled to Azshara searching for a rune, hiring and later betraying several orcish guards of the Horde. [ 35 ] Meanwhile, the night elf Gershala Nightwhisper was worried that by toiling with demonic magic , the blood elves would mutate further than they already did. Wishing to avoid the rise of another vile race of monsters, he studied the brain stems of naga and satyr so that he might deduce what fate the elves were headed toward. [ 36 ]

At some point, the blood elf Lethtendris was drawn to Dire Maul and created a device to gather magical power that siphoned the energies of the place, in order to satisfy her cravings for arcane magic and ultimately destroy her enemies. [ 37 ] Master Telmius Dreamseeker himself was incinerated by Prince Tortheldrin while trying to gain knowledge from the Shen'dralar ancients found within the place. [ 38 ]

In the Blasted Lands , the blood mage siblings Drazial and Lynnore studied fel-corrupted beasts, while Ambassador Ardalan tried to convince the Alliance to put aside their "petty squabbles" with the Horde , and to instead unite against the Burning Legion . [ 39 ]

The Burning Crusade

This section concerns content related to The Burning Crusade .

Silvermoon City , rebuilt by the blood elves.

By Year 26 ADP, siphoning from external sources resulted in the birth of the wretched , disorganized magical addicts who became a reminder to the blood elves of the importance of controlling their magic addiction . [ 40 ] Caught in the throes of constant combat with the Scourge and the Amani trolls , the kingdom of Quel'Thalas needed allies, and the answer came from Sylvanas Windrunner who introduced Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron to the reformed Horde . Despite the elves' history of warfare with the orcs , Lor'themar knew the modern Horde was not the Orcish Horde of the past, and he was painfully aware that time was running out for both his people and his prince. On the other hand, Warchief Thrall and High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof saw great promise in the blood elves who had proved their courage and resolve to protect their kingdom from the Scourge, and both believed that helping the blood elves would be an act of honor: like many races of the Horde, the sin'dorei were a people brought near to extinction and were trapped in a struggle between restoring their once-glorious kingdom and their addiction to magic. This alliance allowed the Horde to gain another foothold on the Eastern Kingdoms and the blood elven mastery of the arcane to their arsenal, while the Horde's support would allow the blood elves to reach their missing prince on Outland. [ 41 ]

Concurrent with failed negotiations with the Alliance , [ 42 ] and night elven incursions into Quel'Thalas, [ 43 ] the neutralization of Dar'Khan Drathir in Deatholme allowed the sin'dorei to take an equal seat at the Horde's political table. [ 44 ] Within sin'dorei society, Grand Magister Rommath and the Magisters quickly went about silencing any dissidents speaking against the new direction Silvermoon was taking, and the blood elves enforced what bordered on a totalitarian police state to better keep their people united.

Kael'thas and his lord Kil'jaeden at the Sunwell .

More blood elves from Quel'Thalas eventually began their travels into Outland, however, what awaited them was not the paradise that was promised, but the barren wasteland of Hellfire Peninsula . After dismantling the Sunfury 's presence in the Netherstorm , the allegiance of Kael'thas to the Burning Legion was uncovered by the Scryers , and the prince himself was cornered in Tempest Keep . After being left for dead, the lord of the blood elves appeared before the naaru A'dal in Shattrath City , berating him for not finishing the job. Announcing his loyalties to all those present, Kael'thas resolved to usher Kil'jaeden into Azeroth . [ 45 ] The mad prince returned to Quel'Thalas and briefly attacked Silvermoon with his felblood minions. Retaking M'uru from its chambers, Kael'thas set the stage for his final stand on the Isle of Quel'Danas . He also spirited Anveena away from her undisclosed location in Quel'Thalas, and leeched both her and M'uru's powers to restore the Sunwell, performing a ritual fortified by the arcane energies harvested from the Netherstorm. [ 8 ] Lady Liadrin witnessed her prince's attack on Silvermoon herself; and now without a power source for the Blood Knights , she traveled to Shattrath to meet with A'dal. She learned that M'uru had resigned himself to this fate a long time ago and pledged the blades of the Blood Knights to ending the prince's dark ambitions and restoring Silvermoon to its glory. [ 46 ]

Silvery moon , washed in blood, led astray into the night, armed with sword of broken Light . Broken, then betrayed by one , standing there bestride the sun. At the darkest hour, redemption comes, in knightly lady sworn to blood .

— Velen 's prophecy

The Shattered Sun Offensive , a coalition of the Scryers' blood elves and the Aldor 's draenei, marched to liberate Quel'Danas. Prior to this turn of events, the prophet Velen foretold the revelations to come, tied to the sin'dorei and their fate. Kael'thas made his final stand in the Magisters' Terrace , little more than a shadow of his former self, reduced to a wretched himself. He was cut down, and the Shattered Sun Offensive took the battle to the Sunwell - now occupied by the most powerful blood elves under Kael's command, the Shadowsword , allowed to gorge themselves upon unlimited fel power, and defeated them, along with their Burning Legion allies. Ultimately, the heroes relieved the Sunwell from the Legion and banished Kil'jaeden back to the Twisting Nether . [ 8 ]

After the encounter involving Kil'jaeden , the Sunwell was once more fouled by corruptive energies. The tainted well threatened to engulf both the blood elves and their kingdom, and Quel'Thalas' regent was forced to consider destroying it, as Kael'thas had done years before. However, Prophet Velen and Lady Liadrin appeared on the scene shortly afterwards, and the draenei prophet presented another solution: Velen recovered M'uru 's heart, alone unblemished in the naaru's fall to the void , and cast the small flickering "spark" into the Sunwell. With that, the Sunwell was cleansed, [ 8 ] and a huge pillar of light emerged from the fount, to which Velen declared: "In time, the light and hope within, will rebirth more than this mere fount of power... Mayhap - they will rebirth the soul of a nation." [ 47 ]

Inspired by the Sunwell's rebirth, the blood elves have since entered into a shining new era in their ancient race's history. Although some elves remained hesitant to abandon their dependence on arcane magic, others embraced change for the betterment of Quel'Thalas. Yet only time would tell if the blood elves can avoid repeating the tragic mistakes of their past. [ 5 ] The blood elves no longer required draining magic to keep in good health, and their crippling addiction is sated once more, if not conquered completely. With the Sunwell's rebirth, the Blood Knights have engaged in a far more harmonious relationship with the Light, which they now channel directly through the Sunwell itself, wielding the Light in a healthy way, instead of dominating it. [ 48 ] [ 49 ] They have resolved to embrace their new source of power, as they forge for themselves a new identity as they lead their people into a more promising future. [ 50 ]

Interregnum

This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels , novellas , or short stories .

Lor'themar Theron , the Regent Lord of Quel'Thalas.

With the betrayal and death of Kael'thas, power passed to his regent, under whom the sin'dorei have turned to for leadership in their prince's place. Resolved to see his people conquer their addiction completely, Lor'Themar spent the following years repairing his kingdom's relations abroad. [ 51 ] Rather than proclaim a new elven dynasty, which he claimed neither he nor any other elf had a right to do, Lor'themar opted to retain his title of regent lord. After the sin'dorei fortified the Isle of Quel'Danas , keeping it well-guarded and not open to visitations, the lord regent attempted to mend bridges with what remains of the high elves , allowing them access to the sacred Sunwell while offering aid and supplies to the Quel'Lithien Lodge . These attempts varied in success, the former making pilgrimages to Quel'Thalas and the latter outright declining any assistance. [ 32 ]

The Sun King's alliance with the Burning Legion, his attack on Silvermoon City to steal M'uru , and pilgrims he forced into harsh labor, [ 52 ] effectively severed the ties of loyalty to the twisted prince for all but the most damningly fanatical sin'dorei. [ 53 ] The Sunfury forces also returned home to fight the Scourge at the borders of the Ghostlands . [ 32 ]

Archmage Aethas Sunreaver later petitioned to formalize involvement with their historical ally, the Magocracy of Dalaran . Unresolved incidents between both nations frustrated negotiations, and while Lor'themar was wary of blood elf citizens entrusting their safety to the Council of Six 's jurisdiction, he also knew many would welcome the chance to rejoin the Kirin Tor as part of the Sunreavers . [ 32 ]

After the Sunwell was restored partly as a font of Light , the Magisters outlawed rituals of the Void in Quel'Thalas, with many embracing its sanctity as the salvation of their kingdom. Some did not observe hypocrisy in their conduct, for certain Magisters had been responsible for M'uru's torture. [ 54 ] A council of Magisters was later assembled to judge Spellbreaker Maella and Magister Umbric , who confessed to pursuing research into the Void despite the interdiction. While Umbric argued that the Void offered their people an additional path to power the blood elves must embrace, for the Sunwell had proved itself corruptible and enforced a stasis that would lead their people to zealotry; Grand Magister Rommath argued that welcoming its corruption was to repeat the mistakes of Prince Kael'thas and Dar'Khan Drathir , and risk the ruin of all the blood elves had struggled to rebuild. Unwilling to disband his followers and destroy his research, Umbric was stripped of his Magister title and exiled. [ 55 ]

Wrath of the Lich King

This section concerns content related to Wrath of the Lich King .

During the war against the Lich King in 27 ADP, the sin'dorei forces accompanied the Warsong Offensive into Northrend . Archmage Aethas Sunreaver , a powerful blood elven member of the Council of Six , was also instrumental in allowing the Horde a sanctuary in the magical city of Dalaran , and his followers, the Sunreavers , sought to have their people admitted as members of the Kirin Tor . [ 32 ]

During the Argent Tournament , Eressea Dawnsinger represented her people as the Grand Champion of Silvermoon, while Malithas Brightblade fought against the adventurers in the Trial of the Champion .

When the Prismatic Blade Quel'Delar was discovered in Icecrown , Blood-Queen Lana'thel of the San'layn shattered it, and both the Sunreavers and Silver Covenant swore to see Thalorien Dawnseeker 's legendary sword restored. [ 56 ] The journey eventually led the adventurers to the Sunwell , and after they purified the reforged blade, Lady Liadrin publicly encouraged her brethren to completely conquer their addiction to magic through the holy fount. [ 57 ]

Cataclysm

This section concerns content related to Cataclysm .

The renewed Sunwell on the Isle of Quel'Danas .

Though relatively unhurt by the Cataclysm in 28 ADP, the blood elves of Quel'Thalas were still dealing with sating their addiction. With the encouragement of Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron , and the renewed Sunwell able to cure their cursed state, a great number have resolved to overcome the magical addiction that had plagued their race, though some were still hesitant to abandon their dependence on arcane magic . [ 58 ] A number of sin'dorei also took a more active role within the wider Horde, such as Master Pyreanor , who served as advisor to Warchief Garrosh Hellscream . [ 59 ]

Under the leadership of High Examiner Tae'thelan Bloodwatcher , an ancient order known as the Reliquary resurfaced to support Quel'Thalas and its Horde allies. With the goal of acquiring powerful magical artifacts for safekeeping and to free the elves of their magical addiction for good, the agents of the Reliquary established themselves as a force to be reckoned with. [ 60 ]

Since their exil from Kalimdor was due to their use of magic, the sin'dorei were outraged to hear that the kaldorei had welcomed the Highborne back and were tolerating the practice of arcane magic again. After witnessing the "rookie" mistakes made by the new kaldorei magi, however, the blood elves were anxiously awaiting whatever mess their distant cousins were going to put themselves in. [ 61 ]

In Winterspring , the Crystal of Zin-Malor addressed the intertwining plights of the Highborne , [ 62 ] their fallen quel'dorei descendants, [ 63 ] and the recent venture of a blood elf Farstrider regiment, all of whom met their end on the icy shores of Lake Kel'Theril . [ 64 ] Their stories were told through the lingering Kaldorei Spirit , Quel'dorei Spirit , and Sin'dorei Spirit .

With the threat of a new troll empire brewing within Zul'Aman , Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing called upon the support Vereesa Windrunner , to which she gladly accepted, though Lor'themar was less than pleased with this decision. A regiment of Farstriders could be found on the outskirts of Zul'Aman, securing the area while Halduron conversed with both the Darkspear chieftain Vol'jin and Vereesa and her Silver Covenant forces. [ 65 ]

Tides of War

This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels , novellas , or short stories .

When Warchief Garrosh Hellscream sought to assault Theramore Isle , the blood elves were viewed as an essential part of the Horde, due in part to their considerable technological advancement, particularly their fearsome mana bomb technology. Having gained favor and respect from the warchief, Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron stated that his people were loyal to the Horde that took them in when no one else would, and that loyalty to Garrosh, being its leader, was a result of that, not the cause. [ 66 ] The Blood Knight Kelantir Bloodblade and two ships of sin'dorei warriors were later sent to support the attack on Theramore. [ 67 ]

Meanwhile, the Sunreavers found themselves undergoing their own intrigues: Aethas Sunreaver and Rhonin chose to allow a contingent of Kirin Tor magi to aid Theramore as a deterrent, [ 68 ] but the mage the two nominated for the task— Thalen Songweaver —was revealed to be Garrosh's spy, with knowledge of the theft of the Focusing Iris . [ 69 ] The latter created a mana bomb for the warchief, which, augmented by the power of the iris, was dropped over Theramore, utterly annihilating it. [ 70 ]

This section concerns content related to Mists of Pandaria .

The Sunreaver Onslaught on the Isle of Thunder .

In Pandaria , sin'dorei history could be seen with Lorewalker Cho , who made observations as he viewed figures of the blood elves, including their high elven forefathers, and their night elven ancestors. The pandaren took special note of the suffering the race had gone through in recent times, the reason behind their moniker, the great power they wield, and the burdens that had come with it. [ 71 ]

During the invasion of Pandaria in 30 ADP, the blood elves joined the Horde 's war effort with Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron himself leading a retinue of Farstriders and Blood Knights . The Reliquary had also been deployed, dispersing to uncover secrets long-hidden on the continent. [ 72 ] However, relations between Quel'Thalas and the Horde become strained due to multiple instances of the blood elves' welfare being disregarded by Warchief Garrosh Hellscream , [ 73 ] culminating in Lor'themar contemplating pulling Quel'Thalas out of the faction and rejoining their old allies of the Alliance . [ 74 ]

While the regent lord and High King Varian Wrynn began the negotiations, however, Sunreavers loyal to Garrosh stole the Divine Bell [ 75 ] and were subsequently expelled by Jaina Proudmoore during the Purge of Dalaran , who then declared the Kirin Tor 's allegiance to the Alliance. In retaliation, Grand Magister Rommath assaulted Dalaran in an effort to rescue Aethas Sunreaver from the Violet Citadel , [ 76 ] as well as many wounded Sunreavers across the city. [ 77 ] [ 78 ] Though Jaina's purge ended the negotiations with the Alliance, Lor'themar was incensed at Garrosh regardless, and later ordered Halduron Brightwing and Rommath to assemble the rangers and magisters, stating that the time had come for the sin'dorei to take matters into their own hands. [ 76 ]

On the Isle of Thunder , the regent lord led the Sunreaver Onslaught from Dawnseeker Promontory ; their assault was directed to counteract the Thunder King and their Zandalari allies, but also to recoup all useful titanic artifacts from the mogu in order to guarantee their survival during the Horde's crisis. [ 79 ] After Horde agents defeated the Dark Animus , Archmage Aethas and his magi uncovered its power source to make functional blood golems of their own. [ 80 ] [ 81 ]

During the Siege of Orgrimmar , after Garrosh and the True Horde were defeated, the regent lord pledged the loyalty of the sin'dorei to Vol'jin as their new warchief. [ 82 ]

During the war in Draenor in 31 ADP, the Sunsworn forces traveled to alternate Draenor under Lady Liadrin 's command, where they they fought with the Auchenai in defense of Auchindoun and Shattrath from the Burning Legion . This section concerns content related to Legion .

Illidari blood elf demon hunter .

While their demonic features and heavy reliance on fel magic have caused them to be frowned upon by their people, their great powers proved invaluable in the battle against the Burning Legion . Following the disastrous Battle for Broken Shore , many blood elves heroes joined the class orders to repel the demons; Ranger-General Halduron Brightwing notably pledged the support of the Farstriders to the Unseen Path , [ 88 ] while Lady Liadrin pledged the Blood Knights to the reformed Order of the Silver Hand . As she turned to address Liadrin, Elisande expressed her disappointment that of all the elves she thought they would understand her choices, but insted, allied with "misfits and monsters". Heritage of the Sin'dorei armor set.
